'''''Solanum villosum''''', also known as the '''hairy nightshade''',<ref>{{PLANTS |id=SOVI8 |taxon=Solanum villosum |access-date=17 November 2015}}</ref> '''red nightshade''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> or '''woolly nightshade''', is a species of sprawling annual weed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Solanum villosum Mill. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:285344-2 |access-date=2025-03-25 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> It is found in Europe, [[western Asia]], northern Africa and is also naturalized in Australia and North America ([https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:285344-2 PoWo Map]).

==Description==
An annual herb, to 70 cm, slightly to densely hairy. The leaf blade is ovate, up to 8 cm long, 3–6 cm wide, entire or shallowly lobed, and petioles to 4.5 cm long. Clusters of 3–8–flowers in the [[inflorescence]]. The [[Corolla (flower)|corolla]] is white or may be purple-tinged. Followed by dull light red or orange-yellow (depending on [[subspecies]]) globular berries, 5–9 mm diam. The seeds are 1.7–2.3 mm long and pale yellow. Compared to ''S. nigrum'', aside from fruit colour the peduncles are moderate (''S. nigrum'' peduncles can become quite long relative to the pedicels).<ref>[http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/efsa/lucid/Solanaceae/Solanum%20species/key/Australian%20Solanum%20species/Media/Html/Solanum_villosum.htm Factsheet ''Solanum villosum'', Flora of South Australia]</ref><ref name="FoT">{{cite book |title=Flora of Turkey and the East Aegean Islands, vol. 7 |author=Davis}}</ref>
